newsitem.title: USA: US official cool to nine-airline air alliance plan.
newsitem.headline: US official cool to nine-airline air alliance plan.

text.p: A key U.S. government official poured cold water Wednesday on the possibility that nine major airlines could form a powerful new global alliance.

An Air Canada official told Reuters in London that nine airlines are forming the alliance to counter the threat posed by the proposed linkup between British Airways and American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp.
But before the alliance could set common air fares it would need antitrust immunity. And it will run into problems there, the U.S. official said.

"The first thing we have to consider is whether we have an 'open sky' agreement with the carriers of the countries," said Patrick Murphy, deputy assistant secretary of Transportation for aviation and international affairs.

"We won't consider granting anti-trust exemptions unless we have an open skies aviation agreement with that country," he said. Such agreements remove restrictions on air service between two countries.
United Airlines, the leader of the new group, already has cleared antitrust problems with Deustche Lufthansa and SAS, because it has an existing agreement with those countries.
And the United States has what Murphy described as a "very liberal, almost open skies" agreement with Canada, which might permit Air Canada in.
But other proposed members would likely run into trouble. Murphy said none of their countries have open skies agreements with the United States.
They are Thai Airways International, South African Airways, British Midland and All Nippon Airways.
